alt: Spatial summation combines different inputs; temporal summation combines repeated inputs close together in time.
caption: Figure 11. Spatial summation combines different inputs; temporal summation combines repeated inputs close together in time.
placed_after: Spatial summation combines effects arriving from different input locations. Inputs separated by a long interval need not add, even if their individual sizes are unchanged.
learner_visual_reading_after: In Figure 11, the left side brings several presynaptic inputs toward one receiving cell. That is a change across locations. Both pictures concern the combined postsynaptic effect, not a taller action potential made by joining several smaller action potentials.

alt: Read down from nervous system to CNS and PNS, then follow the sensory and motor branches. The autonomic branch divides further into sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
caption: Figure 13. Read down from nervous system to CNS and PNS, then follow the sensory and motor branches. The autonomic branch divides further into sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
placed_after: The peripheral nervous system, or PNS, links the brain and spinal cord with receptors, muscles and glands. Sensory pathways carry information toward the CNS; motor pathways carry information away from it. Those words describe direction. The human PNS includes 12 pairs of cranial nerves associated with the brain and 31 pairs of spinal nerves associated with the spinal cord. Nerves can contain fibres with different functions; the name of one nerve does not by itself tell us that every fibre carries the same kind of signal.
learner_visual_reading_after: Read Figure 13 one branching level at a time. The first division is by location: CNS versus PNS. The next peripheral division is by direction: sensory versus motor. Under motor, classify output by target: somatic skeletal-muscle control versus autonomic smooth-muscle, cardiac-muscle and gland control. Finally the autonomic branch separates into sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions. These branching levels answer different questions.
